name: DRMTLGY
description: Direct-to-consumer skincare brand selling serums, tinted SPF moisturizers and eye treatments, marketed with dermatologist-led education and a large affiliate creator program.

evidence.summary: DRMTLGY's own affiliate program page states '15% Commission on Every Sale' and, in the same commission benefit, 'Earn unlimited commissions by sharing your personalized link' — an explicit no-earnings-cap statement on the brand's own program page, so the cap is recorded UNCAPPED. The page also promises performance-based bonuses, milestone gifting and a $55+ average order value.
The page's 'Join DRMTLGY' button routes to drmtlgy.goaffpro.com, so the program is administered on the GoAffPro platform.

The program page is built for creators: it promises creator opportunities including events, virtual masterclasses and dermatologist-led education, plus early access to launches and enhanced sales tracking.

opportunity.title: DRMTLGY Affiliate Program (15% on every sale, unlimited commissions, via GoAffPro)

reasons.niche_fit: Serums, SPF and eye treatments are core skincare-UGC products — routine and before/after content is the brand's whole marketing model.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own program page promises creator events, virtual masterclasses and dermatologist-led education for affiliates.
reasons.compensation: Published 15% on every sale on the brand's own page, with an explicit 'Earn unlimited commissions' statement (verified uncapped), plus performance bonuses and milestone gifting.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email is published on the program page; contact runs through the GoAffPro application.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open join link from the brand's own affiliate page to its GoAffPro registration.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC skincare brand with published program terms on its own store and a stated $55+ average order value.

name: Lashify
description: DIY lash-extension system brand founded by Sahara Lotti, inventor of the original under-lash cluster (Gossamer) system, sold direct to consumers with a creator-first affiliate program.

evidence.summary: Lashify's own Creators page publishes its tiers: everyone starts at 15% on every order through their link or code, rising to 18% (Partner, $1,500 in sales in the last 90 days) and 20% (Icon, $5,000 in the last 90 days). Earnings are paid monthly on the 15th by PayPal (or LashCash store credit with 25% extra). Joining requires at least 10,000 followers on one platform.
The Creators page publishes partners@lashify.com for makeup-artist invitations and for former Affiliate Alliance members migrating to Lashify Creators.

The program is built around creator content: members get lessons on the system and techniques, ready-to-post captions and products to film, and their followers get 2 free lashes on a first order of $100 or more.

opportunity.title: Lashify Creators (15% starting commission, tiers to 20%)

reasons.niche_fit: DIY lash application is one of the most demo-driven beauty categories on TikTok — the product only makes sense in video.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own Creators program supplies lessons, captions and products to film, and replaced its older Affiliate Alliance — a deliberate creator-first rebuild.
reasons.compensation: Published cash commission on the brand's own page — 15% starting, 18% and 20% performance tiers — paid monthly via PayPal.
reasons.contact_access: A published partner email (partners@lashify.com) plus an on-site application; the email route is aimed at makeup artists and migrating affiliates.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application, but gated: creators need at least 10,000 followers on one platform (makeup artists by invitation).
reasons.credibility: Category-defining lash brand with fully published rates, payout timing and level rules on its own site.

name: Bondi Boost
description: Australian haircare brand focused on hair-growth, scalp care and styling tools, sold through its own store and salons, with an affiliate program that rewards posting creators.

evidence.summary: BondiBoost's own collabs page publishes its affiliate terms: 12% commission on every sale through the affiliate's unique link/code, rising to 15% after 60 days with strong engagement, paid monthly, with free shipping for followers. The only stated requirement is posting about the brand at least twice a month.
The collabs page promises monthly prizes for top performers, product restocks for active affiliates and personalized team support — an actively managed creator program, not a dormant listing.

opportunity.title: BondiBoost Affiliate Program (12% base, 15% after 60 days)

reasons.niche_fit: Hair-growth and styling-tool content is a proven hair-UGC category built on routine and progress videos.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own collabs page is creator-facing: a posting rhythm (2x/month), monthly prizes and restocks for active affiliates.
reasons.compensation: Published cash commission on the brand's own page — 12% base rising to 15% after 60 days with strong engagement — paid monthly.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email appears on the collabs page; contact runs through the program application itself.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application on the brand's own collabs page with a simple stated requirement (post twice a month).
reasons.credibility: Established Australian haircare brand with published rates and payout cadence on its own store.

name: Glamnetic
description: Los Angeles beauty brand selling magnetic lashes and press-on nails, built on TikTok Shop creator selling with open and target collaboration commissions.

evidence.summary: Glamnetic's own TikTok Shop terms page documents its standing TikTok Shop commission structure: affiliates earn 15% commission with an open collaboration, 23% with a target collaboration invite (or as a verified Discord member meeting GMV eligibility), and a reduced 5% on posts boosted in its GMV Max ad campaigns; commissions are paid out by TikTok Shop.
The brand publishes tiktokshop@glamnetic.com on glamnetic.com as the contact for its TikTok Shop affiliates.

GRIN's marketplace lists active Glamnetic creator programs (gifting-based campaigns with TikTok and Instagram deliverables) — a separate creator route from the TikTok Shop commission program recorded here.

opportunity.title: Glamnetic TikTok Shop Affiliate Program (15% open collaboration, up to 23%)

reasons.niche_fit: Press-on nails and magnetic lashes are among the highest-converting TikTok Shop beauty demos — application videos are the sales pitch.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand runs its whole growth engine through TikTok Shop creators: published commission tiers, GMV contests with large prizes and a verified-creator Discord community.
reasons.compensation: Published on the brand's own terms page: 15% cash commission on open collaborations, rising to 23% for target collaborations — paid by TikTok Shop.
reasons.contact_access: A dedicated TikTok Shop affiliate email (tiktokshop@glamnetic.com) is published on the brand's own site.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open collaboration on TikTok Shop is available to approved TikTok Shop affiliates without an invite; higher tiers are invite/verification based.
reasons.credibility: Established DTC beauty brand with detailed, legally drafted TikTok Shop program terms published on its own store.

name: Blu Atlas
description: Men's clean skincare and grooming brand (Foundry Brands) selling short-ingredient-list face, hair, body, shave and fragrance essentials made in the USA.

evidence.summary: Blu Atlas's Awin merchant profile publishes a flat 15% commission rate with a 30-day cookie and dedicated affiliate support — the network's own current program terms.
The Awin profile publishes a named affiliate contact for questions or issues: Alice Burnett at Aburnett@foundrybrands.com (Foundry Brands).

An older LinkClicky directory entry (March 2024) listed Blu Atlas at 20% per sale via Impact, which conflicts with the current Awin profile's 15%; the network's own current profile governs, so 15% via Awin is recorded and the older figure is documented as superseded.

opportunity.title: Blu Atlas Affiliate Program via Awin (15%, 30-day cookie)

reasons.niche_fit: Men's grooming is a smaller but fast-growing UGC niche; simple two-step routines suit short-form demo content, and gifting-for-him content widens the creator pool.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The Awin profile markets the program to content partners, but the brand publishes less creator-specific programming than beauty-native rivals.
reasons.compensation: Flat published 15% commission on the network's own merchant profile, with a 30-day cookie.
reasons.contact_access: A named affiliate manager's email is published on the Awin profile — unusually direct access for a network program.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to apply through Awin; approval is at the brand's discretion.
reasons.credibility: Award-winning men's brand (2025 Men's Journal Grooming Awards per its own store) operated by Foundry Brands, with current terms on a major network.

name: Grande Cosmetics
description: Beauty brand known for the GrandeLASH-MD lash enhancing serum and a wider range of lash, brow, lip and hair products with clinically-inspired formulas, sold direct and through major beauty retailers.

evidence.summary: Acceleration Partners, the agency managing Grande Cosmetics' affiliate program, publishes its terms: Hub Commission 10%, 90-day cookies, CPA payout model on the Impact network (Network ID 13069), US consumers, with sub-affiliate/influencer networks among the approved partner types.

Lasso's directory lists Grande Cosmetics at 8% per sale with a 30-day cookie, which conflicts with the program manager's published 10% hub commission and 90-day cookie; the manager's own page governs, so 10% via Impact is recorded.

opportunity.title: Grande Cosmetics Affiliate Program via Impact (10%, 90-day cookie)

reasons.niche_fit: Lash and brow serums are a proven beauty-UGC category built on progress photos and routine videos; the brand's hero product is a repeat-purchase consumable.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The program approves influencer networks and content partners, and the brand works heavily with creators, but publishes little creator-specific programming of its own.
reasons.compensation: Published 10% hub commission from the program's own management agency, with an unusually long 90-day cookie.
reasons.contact_access: No direct affiliate email is published on the fetched pages; contact runs through Impact and the managing agency.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to apply on Impact through the program's published join route.
reasons.credibility: Long-established, retail-distributed beauty brand with a professionally managed program (Acceleration Partners) and published network terms.

name: Loving Tan
description: Australian self-tanning brand selling express tanning mousses, face tans and applicator mitts through its own US store and beauty retailers, long marketed through influencers.

evidence.summary: Loving Tan's own affiliates page offers 'up to 15% commission on each sale (excluding gift cards)' with a 30-day cookie window, bonuses for high-performing affiliates and free samples for select partners. 'Up to 15%' is a ceiling, not a published base rate.

Third-party listings conflict on the actual rate: LinkClicky lists 10% per sale via Impact, FlexOffers lists 4–8% for the US program, and a Katalys-based review cites a 3% default. Because the brand's own page publishes only a 15% ceiling and the listings disagree, commission_rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented.

opportunity.title: Loving Tan Affiliate Program (up to 15% per brand page; base rate unpublished)

reasons.niche_fit: Self-tan application and results content is a staple beauty-UGC format with strong before/after appeal.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand's own affiliates page recruits influencers directly and offers samples to select partners; the brand was built on influencer marketing.
reasons.compensation: The brand publishes only an 'up to 15%' ceiling and third-party listings conflict (3% / 4–8% / 10%), so no base rate can be honestly recorded.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email appears on the fetched program page; sign-up runs through the page's application link.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open application from the brand's own affiliates page.
reasons.credibility: Long-running Australian tanning brand (since 2010) with a US storefront and published program outline on its own site.

name: FOREO
description: Swedish beauty-tech company selling silicone sonic facial cleansing devices (LUNA), smart mask devices (UFO), microcurrent tools (BEAR) and ISSA oral care, sold worldwide through its own store and retailers.

evidence.summary: FOREO's own affiliate program page publishes commissions 'ranging from 2% to 15%', a 60-day cookie window, exclusive offers and a dedicated account manager, with registration via Linkshare (Rakuten Advertising) or HasOffers.

FOREO's own partner blog states its program pays 5–15% per sale through Awin, CJ Affiliate and Rakuten with 30–60 day cookies and no minimum follower requirements. The 5% floor conflicts with the affiliate page's 2% floor, so no single rate is recorded; the published range is 2–15%.

opportunity.title: FOREO Affiliate Program (2–15% published range, 60-day cookie)

reasons.niche_fit: Skincare devices are premium demo products — cleansing, masking and microcurrent routines are natural short-form content with high basket values.
reasons.ugc_evidence: The brand recruits bloggers and creators on its own affiliate page and offers a dedicated account manager, though its program is publisher-led rather than creator-native.
reasons.compensation: Only a wide 2–15% range is published and the brand's own pages conflict on the floor (2% vs 5%), so no base rate can be honestly recorded.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate email appears on the fetched pages; support runs through the network and a dedicated account manager after joining.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open registration via Rakuten/HasOffers, and the brand states there are no minimum follower requirements.
reasons.credibility: Global beauty-tech leader with worldwide retail distribution and long-running network programs on Rakuten, Awin and CJ.

name: Vacation
description: Miami sunscreen brand selling retro-styled SPF lotions, sprays, face sunscreens and fragrances built around its signature 'world's best-smelling sunscreen' scent, sold through its own store and retailers.

evidence.summary: Vacation's Awin merchant profile confirms a live Vacation Inc affiliate program on Awin with a 30-day attribution period; the public profile does not publish a commission rate, so the rate is recorded as null rather than guessed.

Rateful's TikTok Shop analysis (third-party estimates, not brand-published figures) reports that roughly 70% of Vacation's TikTok Shop sales in the 30 days to Nov 6, 2026 came through affiliate creators' videos and LIVEs — evidence of a creator-driven sales model, though no absolute creator count is published, so saturation stays unknown.

opportunity.title: Vacation Inc Affiliate Program via Awin (rate not published)

reasons.niche_fit: Sunscreen with a distinctive scent and retro branding gives creators an easy sensory hook; SPF routines and travel content are steady short-form categories.
reasons.ugc_evidence: Third-party TikTok Shop data attributes roughly 70% of the brand's recent TikTok Shop sales to affiliate creators — the brand sells through creators by design.
reasons.compensation: No commission rate is published on the network profile or any fetched page, so compensation cannot be graded beyond program existence.
reasons.contact_access: No public affiliate contact appears on the fetched profile; contact runs through Awin.
reasons.opportunity_availability: Open to apply through Awin; the brand also sells through TikTok Shop's affiliate system.
reasons.credibility: Well-known, retail-distributed sunscreen brand with an irreverent but established brand identity and a live program on a major network.
